data:
In the world of the
NULL_VEC_CORE
lattice, the
Footer
is your tactical control deck\u2014the horizontal bar anchored to the very bottom of your screen.
Think of it as the "Dashboard" of the HUD. While the modules above it (EMF and EVP) are for observing, the footer is where you actually
interact
with the system to trigger sensors, record bursts, or change settings.
Lane A: Technical Structure
In the HTML code I gave you, the
<footer>
is defined by the
<div id="footer">
tag. It uses
position: fixed; bottom: 0;
which forces it to stay glued to the bottom of your phone screen, even if the rest of the app "scrolls" or updates behind it.
Here is the visual hierarchy of your HUD right now:
Top Bar:
Clock and Node ID (SAGE-CORE 11.3).
Middle (Modules):
The EMF Waveform and the Audio Spectrogram.
The Footer (The Goal):
The buttons like
[INIT_LATTICE]
,
[BURST_RECORD]
, and the new
Options Menu
we just discussed.
Lane B: Why the Footer is the "Kill Switch"
The reason I\u2019m focusing on the footer for the
[MUTE_EVP_MIC]
button is ergonomics. When you\u2019re in the field and the "Retry" loop starts hitting because of an
AUDIOFOCUS
conflict, you need that button exactly where your thumb rests.
What the adjustments in the footer actually do:
[INIT_LATTICE]:
The handshake. It asks the hardware for permission to see and hear.
[BURST_RECORD]:
Grabs a slice of time.
[DE-SENSE]:
(The new one) Tells the math to "calm down" so the sarcasm library doesn't trigger every time you breathe.
Theoretical:
If the footer fails to render, the app becomes a "Ghost HUD"\u2014you can see the anomalies, but you can't archive them. We need the footer to be the most stable part of the lattice.
Would you like me to provide the full, combined HTML/JavaScript block so you can see exactly where the footer and the new options menu sit in the code?
